p1:step: Voyager Therapeutics — TRACER capsid discovery platform / NeuroShuttle has this step in its pipeline: Identification of the cell-surface receptor each BBB-penetrant TRACER capsid engages on brain vasculature, and whether that binding initiates receptor-mediated transcytosis, so capsids with a human-conserved receptor can be nominated as IV-delivered CNS gene therapy vectors (e.g. VY1706 tau-silencing program, ALPL-VYGR-NeuroShuttle). | source: https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/pipeline-overview/ | recorded quote: \"To address this problem, Voyager has discovered novel capsids and identified associated receptors that potentially enable exceptional delivery across the blood-brain barrier following intravenous dosing.\"
p1:activity: Voyager reported Q2 2026 results on 6 August 2026: FDA cleared the IND for VY1706, a TRACER-derived BBB-crossing capsid gene therapy, with dosing expected in Q4 2026; the capsid discovery team presented eight ASGCT 2026 abstracts including receptor-based potency-assay cell lines. | source: https://ir.voyagertherapeutics.com/news-releases/news-release-details/voyager-reports-second-quarter-2026-financial-and-operating/ | recorded quote: \"VY1706 (tau silencing gene therapy): The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared Voyager's Investigational New Drug (IND) application, enabling initiation of a clinical trial in adults with early AD in the United States. Dosing is expected to begin Q4 2026.\"
p1:c1: Receptor mechanism is determined today by RNA-guided in vivo biopanning at library scale: a ~4E7-variant AAV9 peptide-display library is passaged in cynomolgus macaques and reduced to a focused set for further work, by the Capsid Discovery team (Tyler Moyer, Mathieu Nonnenmacher, Todd Carter). | source: https://www.cell.com/molecular-therapy-family/molecular-therapy/fulltext/S1525-0016(25)00373-9 | recorded quote: \"After a second round of in vivo selection, we performed a library enrichment analysis and identified 1,500 variants of interest (Figure 1 A, step 6).\"
p1:c2: Capsid-receptor binding and the pH-release step are measured by surface plasmon resonance at the two pH values of the transcytosis pathway, one pair at a time, rather than by simulation. | source: https://www.cell.com/molecular-therapy-family/molecular-therapy/fulltext/S1525-0016(25)00373-9 | recorded quote: \"We observed direct capsid-receptor interaction in a cell-free assay using surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis with recombinant ALPL, showing that VCAP-102 directly interacts with ALPL with an affinity (K D) of ∼20 nm at pH 7.4 (Figure 4 C).\"
p1:c3: Transcytosis versus retention is decided with a cell-barrier assay, not with molecular simulation. | source: https://www.cell.com/molecular-therapy-family/molecular-therapy/fulltext/S1525-0016(25)00373-9 | recorded quote: \"We established a capsid transcytosis model using Madin-Darby canine kidney cells (MDCK) in a Transwell migration assay.\"
p1:c4: Receptor knowledge is used operationally to build potency-assay cell lines overexpressing the capsid-specific receptor. | source: https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/POSTER_Voyager_ExploitinganAAVCapsidSpecificReceptortoDevelopStableCellLinesforTransductionBasedAssaysforGeneTherapies_May_2026_FINAL.pdf | recorded quote: \"Voyager's discovery of receptors specific for the TRACER TM capsids provides an exciting new avenue to improve transduction and develop proprietary cell lines for assays.\"
p1:done: Voyager has already run the wet-lab analogue of the card's target: the single published pH-resolved capsid-receptor kinetics pair (VCAP-102 binding ALPL at pH 7.4 with rapid dissociation at pH 5.5) plus an ALPL-dependent Transwell transcytosis readout, but it has not published computed pH-resolved MD contact lifetimes classifying transcytosis versus retention across variants. | source: https://www.cell.com/molecular-therapy-family/molecular-therapy/fulltext/S1525-0016(25)00373-9 | recorded quote: \"Rapid dissociation of the ALPL-VCAP-102 complex was observed at pH 5.5 (Figure 4 D), which could point to a mechanism of capsid release on the basolateral side of brain endothelial cells triggered by the acidification of endosomes along the endocytosis/transcytosis pathway.\"
p2:step: Dyno Therapeutics — AI capsid design with BBB-mechanism diversity has this step in its pipeline: The BBB mechanism layer of AI capsid design: determining which blood-brain-barrier transport receptor an engineered capsid engages (human TfR1 for Dyno-yp2, ALPL for Dyno-9zh, or other Dyno-discovered receptors) and whether that engagement is conserved in human orthologues, before capsids are handed to CNS gene therapy partners. | source: https://www.dynotx.com/news/dyno-therapeutics-launches-dyno-yp2-a-top-performing-tfr1-mediated-aav-capsid-to-further-diversify-cns-delivery-portfolio | recorded quote: \"In parallel with its work on TfR1-mediated delivery, Dyno is advancing capsids that engage additional BBB transport pathways, including several BBB-receptors discovered by Dyno, as well as approaches involving alkaline phosphatase (ALPL), a compelling and distinct mechanism with translational relevance across species.\"
p2:activity: Dyno announced two new capsids and AI-platform updates at the ASGCT Annual Meeting on 13 May 2026, including Dyno-9zh which crosses the BBB via ALPL binding, and presented further multi-mechanism data in October 2026. | source: https://www.dynotx.com/news/dyno-therapeutics-launches-two-new-aav-capsids-and-ai-platform-for-rare-disease-therapeutic-development-at-the-2026-american-society-of-gene-cell-therapy-asgct-annual-meeting | recorded quote: \"Dyno Therapeutics, Inc., a genetic technologies company applying artificial intelligence (AI) to solve the grand challenge of in vivo gene delivery, today announced the launch of two new adeno-associated virus (AAV) gene delivery capsids for central nervous system (CNS) and muscular delivery, alongside updated in vivo results for previously released capsids Dyno-yp2 (CNS) and Dyno-bn8 (muscle).\"
p2:c1: Today the capsid-to-mechanism step is anchored in high-throughput in vivo screening at industrial scale rather than in molecular simulation. | source: https://dynotx.substack.com/p/a-computational-leap-over-an-in-vivo | recorded quote: \"Usually, 10,000 to 10 million pooled sequences are screened in mice or non-human primates (NHP) to identify the best-performing capsids in terms of tissue targeting.\"
p2:c2: Design models are trained on in vivo measurement data from NHP experiments, optimized for cross-species translatability among other properties. | source: https://www.dynotx.com/news/dyno-therapeutics-launches-two-new-aav-capsids-and-ai-platform-for-rare-disease-therapeutic-development-at-the-2026-american-society-of-gene-cell-therapy-asgct-annual-meeting | recorded quote: \"Trained on billions of in vivo non-human primate (NHP) measurements, Dyno's platform engineers AAV capsids optimized for selective delivery, liver detargeting, cross-species translatability and manufacturability.\"
p2:c3: Receptor mechanism for a released capsid is validated empirically by binding of the capsid to human and NHP receptor orthologues, not by computing pH-resolved contact lifetimes. | source: https://www.dynotx.com/news/dyno-therapeutics-launches-two-new-aav-capsids-and-ai-platform-for-rare-disease-therapeutic-development-at-the-2026-american-society-of-gene-cell-therapy-asgct-annual-meeting | recorded quote: \"Demonstrates exceptional cross-species performance, through head-to-head comparison across NHPs and mice and validated binding to human Alkaline Phosphatase (ALPL), supporting human translatability\"
p2:c4: Structure-based reasoning is available in Dyno's stack through open-weight protein structure models run on its Dyno Phi agentic platform, which would be the natural insertion point for a computed transcytosis-versus-retention score. | source: https://www.dynotx.com/news/dyno-therapeutics-launches-two-new-aav-capsids-and-ai-platform-for-rare-disease-therapeutic-development-at-the-2026-american-society-of-gene-cell-therapy-asgct-annual-meeting | recorded quote: \"Phi now enables therapeutic developers to run frontier open-weight protein structure models, applying filters and experimentally calibrated reasoning to support genetic medicine development\"
p2:done: Dyno publicly describes sequence- and structure-based generative design plus empirical receptor validation for its BBB capsids, but no public page, paper or repository shows a pH-resolved MD contact-lifetime classification of transcytosis versus retention; whether such a compute experiment has been run internally is not public. | source: https://www.dynotx.com/news/dyno-therapeutics-launches-dyno-yp2-a-top-performing-tfr1-mediated-aav-capsid-to-further-diversify-cns-delivery-portfolio | recorded quote: \"Dyno's novel generative AI models, trained on billions of in vivo measurements, most recently accelerated with NVIDIA hardware and software, using Hopper GPUs on DGX Cloud and libraries such as TransformerEngine, integrate sequence- and structure-based approaches to engineer functional capsids for new and promising BBB-crossing mechanisms with exceptional efficiency.\"
p3:step: Gradinaru laboratory, California Institute of Technology — AAV capsid–receptor mapping program has this step in its pipeline: Unbiased mapping of the human cell-surface and secreted proteins each engineered AAV binds (capsid–receptor interactome on brain endothelium-relevant receptors such as LRP6), plus structural and computational resolution of the capsid–receptor binding site, to explain which engineered capsids cross the BBB and by what binding signature. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52149-0 | recorded quote: \"Here, we adapt an unbiased human cell microarray platform to determine the extracellular and cell surface interactomes of natural and engineered AAVs.\"
p3:activity: The lab continues to publish on AAV capsid–receptor structure and BBB tropism: Brittain et al. in Molecular Therapy (28 March 2026) on the structural basis of liver de-targeting and neuronal tropism of CNS-targeted capsids, after Lin et al. in Cell Reports (31 October 2025) on human CA-IV-targeted AAVs. | source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymthe.2026.03.030 | recorded quote: \"Overall, we provide a framework for using structural information to guide rational engineering of gene delivery vectors to achieve safe and effective delivery.\"
p3:c1: The receptor-discovery step runs at proteome scale: a pooled six-capsid screen against over 6400 human proteins covering more than 90% of the membrane proteome and secretome, with hits deconvoluted per capsid. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52149-0 | recorded quote: \"After these controls, we then tested the six-capsid pool in a full screen of over 6400 proteins, including 6019 human plasma membrane proteins and secreted and cell surface-tethered proteins, as well as 397 heterodimers.\"
p3:c2: Binding signatures are assigned computationally with AlphaFold-Multimer models of capsid peptides against receptor domains, using 5 structural models per peptide — the exact computation the card's check-first test targets. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52149-0 | recorded quote: \"We applied AlphaFold-Multimer to build models of LRP6-AAV interaction complexes, which predicted that the X1 and CAP-Mac VR-VIII peptides bind LRP6 YWTD domain 1 (Fig. 4c).\"
p3:c3: Predicted domain usage is confirmed experimentally by SPR of receptor domain fragments rather than by simulation of contact kinetics. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52149-0 | recorded quote: \"While the cooperative folding of E1 and E2 complicates testing of individual domains, SPR of mouse LRP6 extracellular domain fragments was consistent with the model predictions, with interaction observed for LRP6-E1E2 but not LRP6-E3E4 (Fig. 4d).\"
p3:c4: Structural work is at atomic resolution and used for rational capsid engineering: cryo-EM structures of CAP-B10 and AAV9-X1.1 with AAVR PKD2 at 2.2–2.2 Å guided variant design validated in vivo. | source: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ymthe.2026.03.030 | recorded quote: \"Here, we solved cryoelectron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of CAP-B10 and its complex with the adeno-associated virus receptor (AAVR) domain PKD2, at 2.22- and 2.20-Å resolutions, respectively.\"
p3:c5: Transcytosis relevance is validated in cells and animals (Lrp6 conditional knockout mice, human and macaque primary brain microvascular endothelial cells, hPSC-derived neurons), not by computed contact lifetimes. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52149-0 | recorded quote: \"Finally, we functionally validate LRP6 capsid interactions in vivo in mice, in the human BBB via primary cell culture, and beyond the BBB using human pluripotent stem cell (hPSC)-derived neurons.\"
p3:done: This lab has already run the card's check-first computation and its experimental counterpart — AlphaFold-Multimer of X1 and CAP-Mac peptides against LRP6 domains predicting YWTD domain 1, confirmed by SPR binding LRP6-E1E2 but not E3E4 — but has not published pH-resolved MD contact lifetimes or any replica-MD classifier of transcytosis versus intracellular retention. | source: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41467-024-52149-0 | recorded quote: \"Representative AlphaFold models, from 5 structural models each of X1 and CAP-Mac peptides with up to 20 recycles, predict selective interaction with human LRP6 domain E1 (E1 and E2: teal, E3 and E4: yellow, AAV peptides: purple).\"

# Pipeline

### Advancing transformative medicines  
for neurological diseases.

## Neurologic diseases – which are estimated to impact more than 1 billion people globally – represent a significant burden on those who suffer from them, on their families and communities, and on the healthcare system.

Thanks to significant advances in human genetics and genomics, we now understand the molecular causes of many neurological diseases and know how to target them.

Our pipeline includes medicines targeting the genetics underlying multiple neurological diseases.

MECHANISM / INDICATION

## VY7523

### anti-tau antibody for Alzheimer’s disease

**Indication**: [Alzheimer’s disease](https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/patient-resources/#alzheimers)

**Modality**: monoclonal antibody

**Target**: tau protein. Designed to target unique C-terminal epitope and block the spread of pathological tau, which is closely correlated with disease progression and cognitive decline in Alzheimer’s disease (AD).

**Key Data**: At [AAIC 2022](https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/14_new_POSTER-Voyager_AAIC2022_Liu_tauAb_FINAL.pdf), Voyager presented data demonstrating that an anti-tau antibody delivered intravenously inhibited the spread of pathological tau by >70% in a mouse seeding model. In a single ascending dose study in healthy volunteers, data on VY7523 demonstrated safety, tolerability, and dose-proportional pharmacokinetics as presented at [CTAD 2025](https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Final_CTAD25_Ratti_Elena_VoyagerTherapeutics.pdf). Also at CTAD 2025, Voyager presented the [study design of the multiple ascending dose intravenous dose study](https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Final_POSTER-Voyager_CTAD_Butler_November_2025.pdf).

**Status**: Voyager expects tau positron emission tomography (PET) imaging efficacy data in Q4 2026 from the ongoing multiple ascending dose (MAD) clinical trial in participants with Alzheimer’s disease.

## VY1706

### tau silencing gene therapy program

**Indication**: [Alzheimer’s disease](https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/patient-resources/#alzheimers)

**Modality**: gene therapy: novel TRACER-derived capsid with vectorized anti-tau siRNA

**Target**: intracellular tau

**Key Data**: At [AAIC 2026](https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/science-publications/), Voyager presented 6-month good laboratory practice (GLP) toxicology non-human primate (NHP) data showing VY1706 was well tolerated and resulted in sustained tau protein reduction by up to 75% in key AD brain regions following a single intravenous (IV) dose.

**Status**: Expected to begin dosing in adults with early AD in Q4 2026. [ClinicalTrials.gov](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT07764146?cond=alzheimer%27s%20disease&viewType=Card&term=VY1706&rank=1)

The quote supports the BBB receptor/capsid part and IV dosing. The transcytosis question and human-conserved receptor aren't in the quote. But it's partly supported → PARTIAL? The item also mentions VY1706 and ALPL-VYGR-NeuroShuttle which do appear on the page (pipeline list). I'd say PARTIAL because the receptor identification claim supported, but transcytosis question not stated. Hmm, but the item's core: "Identification of the cell-surface receptor ... and whether that binding initiates receptor-mediated transcytosis". Page says "identified associated receptors that potentially enable exceptional delivery across the BBB following IV dosing". That supports receptor identification and BBB delivery; transcytosis mechanism not mentioned. I'd go PARTIAL.

LEXINGTON, Mass. , Aug. 06, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Voyager Therapeutics, Inc.
(Nasdaq: VYGR), a biotechnology company dedicated to leveraging genetics to treat neurological diseases, today reported second quarter 2026 financial and operating results.
“We view tau as a critical disease-modifying target in Alzheimer’s disease, and we believe recent third-party data validate this hypothesis,” said Alfred W.
Sandrock , Jr., M.D., Ph.D., Chief Executive Officer of Voyager.
“We continue to advance our two tau-targeted programs toward potential inflection points in clinical trials for Alzheimer’s disease before the end of the year, with the tau-targeted antibody VY7523 expected to generate tau PET imaging data and the tau-targeted gene therapy VY1706 expected to begin dosing.”
Second Quarter 2026 and Recent Highlights
* VY7523 (anti-tau antibody): Voyager expects tau positron emission tomography (PET) imaging efficacy data in Q4 2026 from the ongoing multiple ascending dose (MAD) clinical trial in participants with Alzheimer’s disease (AD).
* VY1706 (tau silencing gene therapy): The U.S.
Food and Drug Administration (FDA) cleared Voyager’s Investigational New Drug (IND) application, enabling initiation of a clinical trial in adults with early AD in the United States . Dosing is expected to begin Q4 2026.
* In July, Health Canada cleared Voyager’s Clinical Trial Application (CTA), enabling the inclusion of Canadian clinical trial sites in the study.
* NBIB-‘223 (Friedreich’s ataxia gene therapy): Voyager’s partner Neurocrine Biosciences has stated that it intends to initiate a clinical trial with NBIB-‘223 in H2 2026, pending successful FDA IND clearance.
* Developing Topics poster at AAIC 2026: Voyager presented 6-month good laboratory practice (GLP) toxicology non-human primate (NHP) data showing VY1706 was well tolerated and resulted in sustained tau protein reduction by up to 75% in key AD brain regions following a single intravenous (IV) dose.
* Eight presentations at ASGCT 2026 : Voyager’s presentations included a late-breaking oral presentation on 3-month GLP toxicology data for VY1706, an oral presentation on muscular and neuromuscular capsid variants, and multiple poster presentations.
Anticipated Upcoming Milestones
* Q4 2026: VY1706 expected to begin dosing in adults with early AD
* Q4 2026: VY7523 tau PET imaging data expected in MAD clinical trial in AD
* H2 2026: Neurocrine intends to initiate a clinical trial with NBIB-‘223 for Friedreich’s ataxia, pending successful FDA IND clearance
* Early 2027: Potential for initial acute safety data with VY1706, pending enrollment"

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
- Fetches content from a specified URL
- Takes a URL and optional format as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts to requested format (markdown by default)
- Returns the content in the specified format
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: if another tool is present that offers better web fetching capabilities, is more targeted to the task, or has fewer restrictions, prefer using that tool instead of this one.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in (text, markdown, or html). Defaults to markdown.

function.name: websearch
function.description:
- Search the web using the session's web search provider - performs real-time web searches and can scrape content from specific URLs
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Supports configurable result counts and returns the content from the most relevant websites
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

Usage notes:
  - Supports live crawling modes when available: 'fallback' (backup if cached unavailable) or 'preferred' (prioritize live crawling)
  - Search types when available: 'auto' (balanced), 'fast' (quick results), 'deep' (comprehensive search)
  - Configurable context length for optimal LLM integration
  - Domain filtering and advanced search options available

The current year is 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information or current events
- Example: If the current year is 2026 and the user asks for "latest AI news", search for "AI news 2026", NOT "AI news 2025"

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 8)

livecrawl.description: Live crawl mode - 'fallback': use live crawling as backup if cached content unavailable, 'preferred': prioritize live crawling (default: 'fallback')

type.description: Search type - 'auto': balanced search (default), 'fast': quick results, 'deep': comprehensive search

contextMaxCharacters.description: Maximum characters for context string optimized for LLMs (default: 10000)
